title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
Waymo's autonomous vehicles were deployed in a foreseeable high-traffic event, Fourth of July celebrations in San Francisco, without adequate battery capacity or contingency planning for the congestion that resulted. At least a dozen vehicles became stranded when their batteries drained during extended gridlock near the Golden Gate Bridge, requiring towing and blocking roadways during the event.

The system failed outside the operating conditions it was designed for. Heavy traffic and major road closures created delays that existing battery capacity could not sustain. The failure could have been caught by traffic simulation, battery-reserve protocols, or restricting operations during known high-congestion events.

It is not established whether the vehicle fire or continued operation during fireworks resulted from system failures or user error, or what specific design or operational changes Waymo has since implemented.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
During Fourth of July celebrations in San Francisco on Saturday, multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded after their batteries drained while stuck in heavy traffic following fireworks displays near the Golden Gate Bridge. Video footage showed at least a dozen stationary Waymo vehicles, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up on streets with some requiring towing. The company attributed the issue to major traffic disruptions, high traveler volume, and unplanned road closures that created unexpected congestion. Waymo stated it is evaluating ways to improve resilience during major traffic events.

The incident frustrated residents, with some spending nearly two hours in standstill traffic and others frustrated by stranded driverless cars blocking roadways. One Waymo vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks, though no injuries were reported. A passenger also reported the vehicle continued driving during fireworks displays on the street. Mayor Daniel Lurie's office indicated they would discuss the traffic situation with public and private partners to improve future experiences.
